issue_context.title: WebApplication.CreateBuilder potentially inefficient, results in many file system checks
comments:
Thanks for contacting us.

We're moving this issue to the `Next sprint planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can help us with prioritizing this work. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).

review_comments: Why is this in here vs being in the caller? This can't go into the BCL like this right?

The indexer doesn't really work otherwise after it's newly constructed. The following test would fail if you didn't call `.AddInMemoryCollection()` yourself which I think is a bad experience:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/32926/files#diff-6dcb162a1522a52cc83721420a5af0212db9a6426a75eb91793c49085c0a1221R84-R96

I got the idea from HostBuilder:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b54dbaf9adb2ec068098394b3f73e8e7cd0ec09c/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting/src/HostBuilder.cs#L141-L142
I hear you but you didn't answer my question

> Why is this in here vs being in the caller?

Because it's more usable this way.

> This can't go into the BCL like this right?

I don't see why not. I copied this from the runtime repo.
